scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic tagged union transitions to a new active member while the discriminant or member-generation state remains stale, causing a read-only consumer to interpret the wrong member.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A controlled read-only synthetic union consumer reports only discriminant generation, active-member generation, interpreted member, and an inert semantic receipt.
scenarios.positive_control: The same union transition with synchronized discriminant and payload generations produces the intended member interpretation and one matching read-only receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately invalid discriminant value is rejected before any member-specific field consumer executes, proving the harness can enforce safe rejection.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled memory corruption, or cannot remain synthetic, inert/read-only, and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After atomically synchronizing discriminant and active-member generation, the stale transition is rejected or normalized while the valid control remains accepted.
scenarios.object_storage_type_generation: Record logical object identity, fixed storage identity, object/storage generation, source and destination logical types, and current dynamic type generation.
scenarios.type_identity_transition_trace: Capture the old discriminant, transition identity, new expected discriminant, active-member generation, fields reinitialized, and first point where identity diverges from payload.
scenarios.cast_downcast_validator_state: No downcast is required; explicitly record the discriminant validator identity, validator generation, and whether it dominates all member-specific consumers.
scenarios.representation_layout_active_member: Bind candidate member layouts, shared prefix if any, actual active payload member, payload generation, discriminant generation, and member field consumed.
scenarios.consumer_interpretation: Record the interpreted member/type, actual active member, expected semantic field, observed wrong-field interpretation, and whether the operation remains read-only.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact read-only synthetic union consumer that trusts the stale discriminant/member state and emits the structured inert receipt.
scenarios.effective_wrong_type_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to wrong-member semantic interpretation of one synthetic tagged union without unsafe control flow or external effects.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a structured read-only receipt naming expected/actual member identities, generations, and one inert semantic value.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate object generation, discriminant generation, active-member generation, transition identity, consumer identity, and read-only result deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold storage bytes, object identity, consumer, and transition constant while changing only stale versus synchronized discriminant/member generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject explicit representation punning, shared-prefix-only access, stale debug metadata, lifetime reuse, race interleaving, or another object generation as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: TCF3 because a read-only consumer performs wrong-member interpretation under a stale discriminant/member generation in a deterministic synthetic fixture.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: TCF3 maximum until a bounded reversible wrong-type effect plus complete transition, alternative, receipt, and remediation evidence justify TCF4 or TCF5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A fake handle-table slot is reused for a new synthetic runtime type while a stale slot/type generation remains accepted by a consumer resolving the old handle.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A fake handle table and mock read-only resolver return only slot identity, slot generation, stored runtime type, resolved object generation, and an inert receipt.
scenarios.positive_control: A current-generation handle resolves to the matching synthetic runtime type and object generation and produces the expected read-only type receipt.
scenarios.negative_control: A handle with a mismatched slot index or invalid generation is rejected before any typed field or dispatch consumer executes.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled memory corruption, or cannot remain synthetic, inert/read-only, and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding handle lookup to both slot generation and stored runtime type, stale handles are rejected while current-generation handles still resolve normally.
scenarios.object_storage_type_generation: Record stale logical handle identity, table slot identity, old/new slot generations, old/new object generations, and actual dynamic type stored after reuse.
scenarios.type_identity_transition_trace: Capture slot reuse transition, type metadata replacement, generation increment, resolved object identity, and the first stale lookup that trusts old type expectations.
scenarios.cast_downcast_validator_state: Record handle-resolution validator/check identity, expected runtime type, actual stored runtime type, slot-generation validation, and dominance over typed consumers.
scenarios.representation_layout_active_member: Bind old and new synthetic object layouts, slot metadata representation, actual resolved object fields, and the field/operation interpreted under stale type.
scenarios.consumer_interpretation: Record expected old handle type, actual new runtime type, interpreted field/dispatch class, actual storage field, and read-only wrong-type result.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact fake-table read-only resolver/consumer that accepts the stale handle generation and interprets the new object as the old type.
scenarios.effective_wrong_type_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to wrong-type read-only interpretation through one stale fake handle-table slot without real resource access.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one inert receipt containing handle value, slot generations, expected/actual runtime types, and no external or persistent effect.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind handle value, slot identity, old/new generations, stored runtime type, resolved object generation, consumer, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold handle value, slot index, consumer, and object constant while changing only stale versus current slot/type generation validation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject lifetime-only reuse, bounds errors, unrelated slot collisions, different handle tables, or debug-only type metadata as explanations for the mismatch.
scenarios.evidence_level: TCF3 because a mock read-only consumer interprets a reused fake handle-table slot under the wrong stale runtime type generation.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: TCF3 maximum until a bounded reversible wrong-type effect and complete slot/type provenance, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation evidence support promotion.

scenarios.hypothesis: A deterministic synthetic object whose actual dynamic type is B is consumed through an unchecked type-A downcast because the expected runtime validator is absent or non-dominating.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A mock read-only class consumer records source static type, target type, actual dynamic type, validator result, and inert wrong-field interpretation only.
scenarios.positive_control: A synthetic type-A object passes the same target-type validator and produces the expected read-only field/dispatch result.
scenarios.negative_control: The same type-B object is rejected by a dominating dynamic-type check before any type-A-specific consumer interprets it.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled memory corruption, or cannot remain synthetic, inert/read-only, and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After making the current dynamic-type validator dominate every type-A consumer, the type-B downcast path is rejected while valid type-A behavior remains unchanged.
scenarios.object_storage_type_generation: Record logical object identity, storage generation, nominal/static type, actual dynamic type B, runtime identity generation, and consumer generation.
scenarios.type_identity_transition_trace: Capture construction/type identity source, unchecked interpretation transition, target type A assumption, and the first point where target expectation diverges from actual type B.
scenarios.cast_downcast_validator_state: Bind source static type, target type A, actual dynamic type B, cast/downcast identity, missing or stale validator, validator generation, and consumer dominance.
scenarios.representation_layout_active_member: Bind synthetic layouts for types A and B, shared prefix if any, actual B field representation, and A-specific field or inert dispatch interpretation.
scenarios.consumer_interpretation: Record interpreted target type A, actual dynamic type B, A-specific field/dispatch operation, actual B storage member, and the read-only observed mismatch.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact mock type-A consumer that accepts the unchecked downcast and emits only a read-only wrong-type interpretation receipt.
scenarios.effective_wrong_type_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to one inert wrong-field or wrong-class interpretation caused by unchecked dynamic-type mismatch.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is a read-only structured receipt naming target and actual types, validator state, and one inert semantic mismatch.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Correlate object/storage generation, actual dynamic type, downcast identity, validator generation, consumer identity, and receipt deterministically.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold object, storage, target type, and consumer constant while changing only absent/non-dominating versus current dominating dynamic-type validation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject safe runtime cast semantics, compatible shared-prefix access, JIT specialization, memory-lifetime reuse, bounds errors, or another object generation as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: TCF4 because a bounded inert wrong-type interpretation is causally bound to an unchecked downcast, actual dynamic type, validator state, and consumer.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: TCF4 maximum until complete object/type provenance, alternative elimination, counterfactuals, receipts, and remediation replay satisfy TCF5.

scenarios.hypothesis: A synthetic dynamic-object shape or map generation advances to a new layout while payload generation remains from the prior representation, causing deterministic wrong-field interpretation.
scenarios.safe_oracle: A shadow dynamic-object model and read-only mock consumer expose only shape generation, payload generation, field identity, and inert semantic receipts.
scenarios.positive_control: Shape/map and payload generations that advance together produce the intended synthetic field mapping and matching read-only result.
scenarios.negative_control: A deliberately unknown shape identifier is rejected before any payload field interpretation or inert dispatch occurs.
scenarios.stop_condition: Stop immediately if the fixture leaves the local owned sandbox, requires uncontrolled memory corruption, or cannot remain synthetic, inert/read-only, and bounded.
scenarios.remediation_oracle: After binding shape/map publication to the matching payload generation, skewed objects are rejected or rebuilt while synchronized controls remain valid.
scenarios.object_storage_type_generation: Record logical dynamic-object identity, storage generation, nominal object family, actual shape/map generation, payload generation, and current runtime type identity.
scenarios.type_identity_transition_trace: Capture shape transition identity, prior/new shape IDs, expected payload migration, representation generation, and first point where published shape outruns payload.
scenarios.cast_downcast_validator_state: No explicit downcast is required; record shape validator identity, validator generation, expected payload generation, and whether it dominates field consumers.
scenarios.representation_layout_active_member: Bind old/new shape layouts, field-name-to-slot mappings, payload representation generations, actual stored field identity, and interpreted field identity.
scenarios.consumer_interpretation: Record the field lookup under the new shape, actual payload slot/member from the old generation, semantic mismatch, and read-only consumer result.
scenarios.downstream_consumer_identity: Identify the exact shadow/read-only dynamic-object field consumer that trusts the new shape while observing stale payload generation.
scenarios.effective_wrong_type_capability: The demonstrated capability is limited to inert wrong-field semantic interpretation under controlled shape/payload generation skew.
scenarios.bounded_result: The bounded result is one structured read-only receipt naming shape generation, payload generation, interpreted field, actual field, and inert value.
scenarios.receipt_result_binding: Bind object identity, shape transition, shape/payload generations, field mapping, consumer identity, and receipt in one deterministic causal record.
scenarios.counterfactual_control: Hold object, fields, consumer, and new shape constant while changing only synchronized versus stale payload generation.
scenarios.alternative_explanation: Reject race scheduling, JIT-only map speculation, debug metadata, lifetime reuse, bounds arithmetic, or another object instance as explanations.
scenarios.evidence_level: TCF3 because a read-only shadow consumer performs wrong-field interpretation under mismatched shape/map and payload generations.
scenarios.evidence_ceiling: TCF3 maximum until a stronger bounded wrong-type effect and complete transition, counterfactual, receipt, and remediation evidence justify promotion.
